title: Raytheon's $24.4B SM-6 Blitz as Yemen's Government Opens a Full Offensive Against the Houthis
subhead: The Pentagon locks in another multiyear missile megadeal to rebuild depleted stockpiles, while Riyadh's Yemeni allies launch a campaign to retake the Red Sea coast and China expands military AI and drone education at its academies.

sections.heading: Raytheon Lands Up to $24.4B for SM-6 as Munitions Megadeals Stack Up
sections.body:
The U.S. Navy awarded RTX's Raytheon unit a multiyear contract worth up to $24.4 billion to produce Standard Missile-6 interceptors, Reuters reported via Defense News on Oct. 1. The five-year deal carries two additional option years and is intended to guarantee a steady supply of the SM-6, a weapon Raytheon says is the only combat-proven missile able to perform anti-air warfare, anti-surface warfare and ballistic missile defense.

The award is the latest in a run of large munitions contracts the Pentagon has pushed this year to force faster output. It follows a $20.7 billion provisional multiyear deal for Raytheon's AMRAAM air-to-air missiles in late September and a $58.6 billion Patriot interceptor deal with Lockheed Martin in July. According to Defense News, these agreements are designed to entice contractors to surge production as part of a broader Trump administration push to prioritize weapons output over shareholder returns.

Industry executives have warned that Congress has not yet appropriated funding for the deals, meaning contractors may be unable to invest at scale in components and facilities until lawmakers act.
sections.whyItMatters: The Pentagon is converting one-time procurement into industrial policy: multiyear commitments meant to expand production lines for interceptors the U.S. has burned through in the Middle East. The unfunded nature of the deals is the catch — commitments without appropriations may not convert into real capacity.

sections.heading: Yemen's Saudi-Backed Government Launches Offensive to Roll Back the Houthis
sections.body:
Yemen's internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government said on Sunday it was launching a major military campaign to recapture all territory held by the Iran-backed Houthis. 'The country's armed forces would press the offensive until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia,' President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address, according to Reuters via Defense News. A military spokesman called on the Houthis to lay down their weapons.

The Houthis (Ansar Allah) have held Sanaa and much of the northwest since 2014, and last month captured the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait and roughly 90 miles of Red Sea coast in a lightning advance. Regional and Western officials told Reuters that Saudi Arabia would lead aerial combat and Yemeni forces would fight on the ground, with more than 100,000 Yemeni troops potentially mobilized depending on scale. The U.S. is providing intelligence support, while some regional and European states are supplying mainly defensive aid, per Reuters.

As the announcement was made, the Houthis claimed ballistic missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area, saying they caused major fires in response to what they described as 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen over 12 hours. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia. The Houthis have also made gains near Taiz, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden, military sources said.
sections.whyItMatters: This escalates the Yemeni civil war into a direct Red Sea shipping fight tied to the wider Iran war. Whoever controls Bab el-Mandeb holds leverage over a route that has gained strategic weight as an alternative to the effectively closed Strait of Hormuz.

sections.heading: China Expands Military AI and Drone Education as Tsentr-2026 Ties Tighten With Russia
sections.body:
China's People's Liberation Army is setting up new military academy colleges dedicated to AI, drones and discipline, according to the South China Morning Post (Oct. 2), signaling a push to institutionalize skills around unmanned and intelligent warfare. The move comes as Chinese troops took part in Russia's Tsentr-2026 exercise, a mass drill involving tens of thousands of personnel from Shanghai Cooperation Organisation countries that Moscow says was used to apply lessons from the Ukraine war, SCMP reported on Oct. 3.

Separately, SCMP reported on Oct. 1 that U.S. munitions shortfalls — particularly for HIMARS and related missiles — raise the stakes in any Taiwan Strait contingency, noting China's defense industry appears to be operating at an elevated tempo. Taiwan is set to receive all 29 HIMARS systems from its initial orders by the end of this year, with another 82 approved for purchase.

SCMP also reported the U.S. claims its F-47 will be the first sixth-generation jet, while China's J-36 and J-50 are already flying.
sections.whyItMatters: China is moving on two fronts at once — formalizing military AI and drone expertise through its academies and deepening live interoperability with Russia. The industrial tempo contrast with Western stockpile shortfalls is the part Western planners are watching most closely.

sections.heading: France Bets on Sovereign AI for Its 'Loyal Wingman' Push
sections.body:
France's Air Force, working with the Directorate General for Armament and the defense AI agency Amiad, plans to fly crewed fighters in collaboration with combat drones in 2028 under a project called Hypairion, Defense News reported on Oct. 2. Col. Cédric, head of the Air Force capability-development office, said the aim is to equip platforms with open, modular architectures owned by the government rather than proprietary systems.

The Air Force is converting two Mirage 2000 fighters at Mont-de-Marsan airbase into AI test beds, with testing of 'all kinds of use cases' to begin by the end of the year. Early use cases include AI-assisted flight-path optimization and tactical decisions such as when to deploy air-to-air or air-to-ground weapons. The DGA has set a 2033 target for the first version of the Rafale F5 standard.

Unlike company-driven loyal-wingman efforts by Airbus, BAE Systems, General Atomics and Anduril, the French project keeps critical technology under state control, with Amiad providing sovereign AI for command and control and mission autonomy.
sections.whyItMatters: France is staking out a state-owned model for military AI at a time when most Western collaborative-combat-aircraft work is contractor-led. If it holds, it becomes a template for European sovereign autonomy in the AI layer of air combat.

sections.heading: Pentagon Eyes Space-to-Space Tracking With GHOST-R Satellites
sections.body:
Space Systems Command awarded prototype contracts to Northrop Grumman and four-year-old True Anomaly under the Geosynchronous High-Resolution Optical Space-Based Tactical Reconnaissance program, or GHOST-R, on Sept. 18, Defense News reported. The program aims to deliver high-resolution 'space-to-space imagery' of objects more than 22,000 miles above Earth in geostationary orbit.

Northrop will deliver a small-suitcase-sized prototype built on its ESPASat-L spacecraft with a commercial optical sensor on an accelerated 24-month timeline. True Anomaly will provide its Jackal autonomous orbital vehicle and Mosaic command-and-control system. Both companies already hold Space Force contracts tied to the Golden Dome missile defense initiative. The prototypes are set to launch to geosynchronous orbit by 2028 and fly government-owned missions by 2029. The contract value and funding source were not disclosed.
sections.whyItMatters: Space Domain Awareness is shifting from a handful of exquisite satellites to low-cost, maneuverable commercial-derived platforms. GHOST-R is a concrete step in building the tracking layer that missile-defense and counter-satellite operations would depend on.

sections.heading: Italy's Defense Windfall Shrinks by Up to EUR8 Billion
sections.body:
Italian military planners risk losing out on about EUR8 billion ($9 billion) in funding as government and opposition parties move to cut defense spending and Ukraine support, Defense News reported. The shortfall is tied to Italy's use of the EU's 'National Escape Clause,' which lets states exempt some defense spending from deficit calculations.

At a Cabinet meeting, deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini, who leads the League and opposes defense hikes and Ukraine military aid, pushed the expected windfall down to around EUR14 billion from an earlier estimate of EUR21-22 billion. A government source said the reduction was agreed but not yet final. Meloni has committed to NATO's 5% of GDP target and claims Italy reached 2.8% this year including domestic security spending, though this year's budget breakdown has not been published. Rome also said in August it would request EUR8 billion in EU SAFE loans, down from an original EUR14.9 billion.

Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani told a parliamentary hearing he is a strong supporter of SAFE loans, noting Portugal is buying FREMM frigates built by Leonardo and Fincantieri with SAFE funds.
sections.whyItMatters: Italy is a test case for whether Europe's rearmament financing mechanisms survive domestic political fatigue. A shrinking escape-clause windfall directly limits how much Rome can commit to procurement and to programs like the FREMM sales Leonardo is counting on.

sections.heading: Munitions and Industrial Base Notes: Tungsten, PrSM and Carrier Overhaul
sections.body:
Defense industrial base moves continue across the U.S. The Pentagon announced a $450 million investment in The Elmet Group to strengthen the domestic supply chain for the critical mineral tungsten, Defense News reported. The U.S. Army selected five companies — Anduril, Castelion, Lockheed Martin, Mach Industries and RTX — to develop advanced long-range missile prototypes under the Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) effort. The carrier USS Harry S. Truman is slated for a $5.1 billion mid-life overhaul. Boeing also received a roughly $85 million contract for four more MH-139A Grey Wolf helicopters, its first under full-rate production.

In the drone space, Neros and Perennial Autonomy scored highest in the second phase of a Pentagon competition to find producers of high-quality, low-cost commercial drones, Defense News reported, reflecting continued effort to diversify away from a handful of suppliers.
sections.whyItMatters: These are the unglamorous inputs — raw materials, prototyping, depot maintenance and drone suppliers — that determine whether the megadeals above can actually be produced at scale. Tungsten in particular points to a supply-chain vulnerability the Pentagon is now funding directly.

bottomLine: The day's clearest signal is that the U.S. is locking in multiyear missile production at enormous scale — $24.4 billion for SM-6 on top of the AMRAAM and Patriot deals — betting that multiyear commitments, not annual orders, can rebuild depleted interceptor stockpiles, though the money remains unappropriated. In Yemen, the Saudi-backed government's launch of a full counteroffensive turns the Red Sea into a direct contest over Bab el-Mandeb, compounding pressure from the already-closed Strait of Hormuz. Elsewhere, China is institutionalizing military AI and drone expertise and drilling alongside Russia, France is building a state-owned AI wingman model, and Italy's shrinking defense windfall shows Europe's rearmament financing is colliding with political fatigue.
sources: Defense News/Reuters, Defense News (Navy SM-6 award), Reuters via Defense News (Yemen offensive), Defense News (Saudi Red Sea assault plan), Defense News (France Hypairion), South China Morning Post, Defense News (GHOST-R space satellites), Defense News (Italy defense spending), Defense News (tungsten/PrSM/Grey Wolf/drone competition)
